Jordan — quick finance take:

- Net terms: our standard is Net 45. We can accommodate Net 60 for strategic deals but only if we mitigate credit risk. For a POC I recommend either a 20–30% upfront deposit or invoice the first month up front and the remainder Net 45.
- Currency: invoicing in EUR is fine. If they want USD we should treat as a separate priced order with FX variance clause. Avoid mixing currencies on one invoice — it complicates AP/AR.
- Commit tranches: we can map the 3‑tranche model to three invoices tied to milestones (Kickoff / Midpoint / Close). That matches revenue recognition and keeps cashflow predictable.
- Withholding: if they indicate any withholding at source we need signed tax forms and evidence of any treaty benefits. Otherwise we treat taxes as customer responsibility; include a gross‑up clause only if finance/legal approve.

I'll draft a short billing ops note with recommended language for payment schedule and FX handling.

Ben

Thanks for the context. Legal take (high level):

- VAT / reverse charge: fine to accept reverse charge provided FinPulse supplies a valid EU VAT ID and includes the VAT ID on the PO. Add a representation and indemnity paragraph: customer represents VAT registration and will self‑account for VAT; customer indemnifies Redwood if local tax authorities assess VAT due to customer's failure to self‑account.
- Net terms & deposit: ok to accept Net 60 for the first invoice if we secure a deposit (20–30%). For subsequent invoices keep Net 45. Add language allowing Redwood to suspend service for past‑due amounts after 30 days.
- Invoice split & itemization: accept their PO template but include an appendix in the MSA that lists line items and invoicing cadence. Prefer separate invoices per currency to limit FX exposure.
- Withholding / gross‑up: do not agree to gross‑up automatically. If they insist, require proof of withholding law and provide a capped gross‑up with evidence; otherwise taxes remain customer's responsibility.

I've uploaded a marked‑up version of the order form with tracked commercial redlines. Key additions: VAT representation/indemnity, payment milestones, suspension right, currency clause, and reference to MSA appendix.

Kim
